script.title: A Volcano Buried Pompeii and Saved Its Graffiti
sentences: A Roman town vanished under up to six metres of ash.
That was Pompeii, near Naples, buried when Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD.
Then the city stayed largely undisturbed until its rediscovery in the late 16th century.
Major digging only began in the mid-18th century, and early efforts were marred by looting.
People had scratched graffiti on walls, inside rooms and out, in the casual Latin of the street.
That everyday spoken Latin is otherwise largely lost.
In Pompeii, the vandals ended up keeping the record.
script.description:
Vesuvius buried Pompeii in 79 AD under metres of ash.
Its wall graffiti kept the everyday Latin Romans actually spoke.
claims_en: Pompeii was buried under 4 to 6 metres of volcanic ash and pumice.
It was buried in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD.
It had 10,000 to 20,000 residents at the time it was destroyed.
Pompeii remained largely undisturbed until its rediscovery in the late 16th century.
Major excavations did not begin until the mid-18th century.
Initial efforts were haphazard or marred by looting.
Numerous graffiti carved on outside walls and inside rooms provide examples of the Vulgar Latin spoken colloquially at the time.
That colloquial Vulgar Latin is largely lost.
